name: Why the Crossing Is Here

levels.entry: The sea between the shores is a mile or so. East of here it opens and does not close again.
Both headlands are the same black-and-grey stone in the same courses, tilted the same way.
They are one hill with the middle gone. The strait is where it broke, not where it was cut.
And the islands are the middle. Two pieces of the same hill, still up, which is the thing nobody here says out loud because it is obvious to them.

notes: Aravali. Four rungs rather than five: this one answers.
